mission.finding: The recovery package distinguishes the consumed V1 auth failure from a separately versioned V2 gate without changing the data estimand.

flexibility.finding: V1 and V2 profiles share the adapter seam while retaining distinct owner phrases and ignored roots.

compatibility_history.finding: The V1 run and negative evidence remain immutable; V2 cannot consume the V1 root.

efficiency.finding: The patch wraps existing TASK-08 transport and adds no dependency, scheduler or generic service.

research_truth.finding: Auth rejection, missing capture, UNKNOWN and technical observations remain distinct from empty/zero/settled claims.

secret_handling.finding: No provider key or raw bytes are added to tracked artifacts; the future phrase grants no current authority.

owner_operability.finding: A later V2 external action still needs one exact owner phrase after exact-main CI; this package does not run it.

monitoring_recovery.finding: Separate create-only roots and terminal validation prevent silent retry or cross-run reuse.

reuse_first.finding: No second socket implementation is introduced.

execution_to_cashflow.finding: No execution, inventory, settlement, PnL or NetReturn authority exists.

falsifiers: offline tests read credentials or call transport
technical capture becomes trial or zero-volume claim

now.value: Resolve whether the first failure was only access state or a deeper stream feasibility problem.
now.evidence: V2 offline package and deterministic tests; no second provider action yet.
now.cost_risk: One separately authorised foreground attempt under frozen caps.
now.activation_trigger: Exact-main CI pass and explicit V2 owner phrase.
now.why: It is the cheapest next discriminator after the closed V1 auth failure.

watch.value: Only useful if a valid first capture shows coverage or cadence is the bottleneck.
watch.cost_risk: Adds quota, monitoring and reconciliation burden.
watch.activation_trigger: First valid capture proves repeatability/coverage gap.
